title: Lipschitz-Margin Certificates as Runtime Safety Monitors for BCI-Controlled Effectors
summary: This proposal turns per-instance robustness certificates into a runtime monitor that stops a BCI from issuing a command when it cannot be certified. For each EEG trial, a certified radius is computed from the logit margin and a precomputed SDP Lipschitz bound, or from the instance-specific Cross-Lipschitz bound. When the radius falls below a threshold set to the noise level, the system abstains instead of driving an assistive device. The monitor would be compared with Mahalanobis- and cosine-distance adversarial detectors. Tests would cover white-box attacks, universal perturbations, unseen attacks, and natural artifacts. The aim is to test whether certificates generalize to unknown threats better than learned detectors.
gap: Existing EEG adversarial detectors are statistical and learned. They perform well on white-box attacks they were tuned for, but transfer less reliably to unknown attacks, and they give no guarantee. The safety and neurosecurity literature calls for monitoring and safe failure in BCIs that control physical effectors, but no cited work links formal robustness certificates to abstention decisions in BCIs.
approach: Precompute global or layer-wise SDP Lipschitz bounds for the trained decoder. At inference, compute the instance-specific certified radius, which can also be combined with local gradient-norm estimates, and abstain when it is below a threshold tau. Tau is calibrated on clean validation data to meet a target false-abstention rate. A simulated closed-loop cursor or effector task would measure how often unsafe commands get through.
evaluation: Baselines: Mahalanobis and cosine-distance detectors, softmax-confidence thresholding, and no monitor. Measures: detection AUC against PGD, FGSM, universal and natural-artifact perturbations, including transfer to attacks not seen during calibration; risk-coverage curves; rate of unsafe commands let through in simulated control; and computational latency. Evaluation would span several MOABB datasets and EEGNet and ShallowConvNet.
